title: Coraline
author: Neil Gaiman
short_summary: When Coraline Jones explores her family's new flat, she finds a small door that leads to an eerie "Other" version of her world, ruled by an Other Mother with black buttons for eyes. At first the Other world seems better than her real one — until Coraline realises her parents have been taken and that three children before her never got out. To free them she has to make a bargain with something that has no intention of playing fair.
extended_summary:
Coraline's family moves into a flat in a big old house. Downstairs live two retired actresses, Miss Spink and Miss Forcible, who read her tea leaves, tell her she is in danger and give her a stone with a hole in it. Upstairs lives an old man who says he is training a mouse circus. Coraline's own parents are busy and distracted, and when she opens the locked door in the drawing room she finds only a brick wall behind it.

One day the bricks are gone. Down the corridor is a flat exactly like hers, with an Other Mother and Other Father who cook what she likes, play with her, and have black buttons sewn where their eyes should be. They want her to stay — she need only let them sew buttons onto her own eyes. When Coraline refuses and goes home, her real parents have vanished, and in a mirror she sees them trapped and waving.

Behind a locked door Coraline finds the ghosts of three children the Other Mother took long ago, whose souls she stole and then discarded. Coraline goes back and challenges the Other Mother to a game: if she can find the three souls and her parents, they all go free; if she loses, she stays and gets buttons. Using the stone with the hole to see what is hidden, she wins — escapes with the snow globe her parents are trapped in by throwing the cat at the Other Mother — and then has to deal with one last thing: the beldam's severed hand, still crawling after the key. Coraline lures it out to a deep old well and drops it in.

questions.prompt: The very first time Coraline unlocks the little door in the drawing room, what does she find behind it?

options: A brick wall where the corridor used to be
A dark corridor smelling of damp and dust
A staircase going down into the cellar
A cupboard with the old tenants' coats in it

questions.explanation: Her mother shows her the bricks precisely to prove there is nothing there. That is what makes the second opening so frightening: Coraline has already seen the wall with her own eyes, so when the corridor appears she knows something has changed rather than that she has been mistaken.

questions.prompt: What is the one thing that always gives away the people in the Other world, however friendly they seem?

options: Black buttons sewn where their eyes should be
Their voices come a moment after their lips move
They cast no shadow at all in the lamplight
Their hands are always colder than a person's

questions.explanation: Gaiman puts the horror in plain sight from the first minute, which is braver than hiding it. The buttons are also the price: Coraline can stay in a world that suits her perfectly, so long as she lets someone sew over the way she sees.

questions.prompt: Miss Spink gives Coraline a small stone with a ___ in it, and tells her it is good against bad things.
questions.explanation: It is an adder stone, an old piece of country folklore, and it works: looking through the hole lets Coraline see what the Other Mother has hidden. Two forgetful old ladies with a teapot turn out to have given her the only tool she needs.

questions.prompt: Coraline finds the ghosts of children the Other Mother took long before her. How many are there, and what did the Other Mother take from them?

options: Three children, whose souls she stole and discarded
Two children, whose names she took and forgot
Four children, whose shadows she keeps in a jar
Three children, whose voices she sewed into a doll

questions.explanation: They were loved, then used up and thrown away, and they cannot even remember their own names. Their fate is what turns Coraline's escape into a rescue: she could simply leave with her parents, and she does not.

questions.prompt: Put the events of Coraline's story in the order they happen.

items: Coraline is shown a brick wall behind the little door
She walks down the corridor and meets the Other Mother
She comes home to find her real parents gone
She challenges the Other Mother to a game with rules
She throws the cat and escapes with the snow globe
She drops the crawling hand into a deep well

questions.explanation: The shape of the book is that Coraline goes through the door three times: once out of boredom, once to see, and once on purpose to fight. Notice that the story does not end with the escape — the last danger comes after she thinks she has won.

questions.prompt: Match each character to what they do for Coraline — or to her.

right: Read the tea leaves and hand over a protective stone
Claims to be training mice to perform in a circus
Can speak on the other side and needs no name
Crawls after the key long after its owner is gone

questions.explanation: The adults in the real world are ridiculous and largely useless — and yet the stone works and the warning was true. The cat, who refuses to be named because cats know who they are, is the only ally who understands the Other world from the start.

questions.prompt: Sort each detail by which world it belongs to.

options.label: Parents too busy with work to play with her
A recipe she does not want to eat
A cat that watches her but never speaks
Exactly the food she likes, every time
Toys in the box that move by themselves
Nothing but white mist beyond the house

questions.explanation: The Other world is built out of Coraline's own complaints, which is why it is so tempting — and the mist is the giveaway. The beldam can copy anything Coraline has noticed and nothing she has not; the world stops where her attention stops.

questions.prompt: Coraline offers the Other Mother a game: find the souls and her parents, and everyone goes free. Why does the Other Mother accept a bet she could simply refuse?

options: She cannot resist a game, and expects to win easily
She is bound by a promise made to the ghost children
The cat forces her to agree to Coraline's terms
She has to let a guest ask for one thing each day

questions.explanation: Coraline works out that the creature is vain and bored, and that being challenged is the one thing it will not walk away from. It is the cleverest move in the book: she cannot beat the Other Mother by strength, so she uses the only weakness a predator that plays with its food has.

questions.prompt: The Other world gives Coraline everything she had been wishing for: attention, good food, interesting toys, parents who listen. If you had found that door, would you have been tempted to stay a while — and what, exactly, should have warned you? Give your reasons.
questions.explanation: There is no single right answer and honesty about temptation should be rewarded. A strong answer names at least one specific warning sign from the book — the buttons, the mist where the world ends, the doll-like other neighbours, the children's ghosts — rather than only saying 'it was creepy'. Both 'I would have stayed a while' and 'I would have run' can score full marks.

questions.prompt: The Other world copies the real one almost perfectly, but always gets one thing wrong. Invent an Other version of one room you know well. What would be better about it, and what single detail would tell you that something is wrong?
questions.explanation: There is no single right answer. A strong answer has both halves — something genuinely tempting, and one small wrong detail — because that pairing is exactly how Gaiman builds fear. An answer that is only frightening, with nothing attractive about it, has missed how the Other world works.

questions.prompt: Coraline works out that her real parents are being held inside a ___ standing on the mantelpiece.
questions.explanation: It is an ordinary ornament she has walked past several times. The Other Mother's cruelty is always domestic: parents in a paperweight, souls behind a mirror, a hand under the sofa.

questions.prompt: Coraline has escaped and her parents are safe — but the danger is not over. What does she finally do about the Other Mother's severed hand?

options: Lures it out and drops it down a deep well
Burns it in the fireplace of the drawing room
Locks it in the cellar behind the little door
Gives it to the cat to carry away and bury

questions.explanation: She sets up a picnic on the boards over an old well, waits for the hand to come for the key, and lets it fall. Coraline does not defeat the last of the beldam by being brave but by being careful — she plans it, in daylight, on purpose.
